The six terms are exactly the off-diagonal terms of the product $(a+b+c)\left(\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}\right)$. Expanding this product gives

$$(a+b+c)\left(\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}\right) = 3 + \frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{a}+\frac{a}{c}+\frac{c}{b}+\frac{b}{a}.$$

The diagonal terms $\frac{a}{a}, \frac{b}{b}, \frac{c}{c}$ contribute 3, and each remaining term $\frac{x}{y}$ with $x \ne y$ appears once.

Substituting the given values:

$$\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{a}+\frac{a}{c}+\frac{c}{b}+\frac{b}{a} = 26 \cdot 28 - 3 = 728 - 3 = 725.$$

ANSWER: 725
